text:
Sarah (support): Hey team, incoming customer escalation from Clipper — they see a 2x p99 latency jump for LLM generate calls since ~08:20 UTC. Customer claim vs our public dashboard mismatch :confused:

Jason (sre): Can you paste a request_id + sample timestamps? Which dashboard are they looking at?

Sarah (support): request_id=clip-req-20240422-9b7f3, observed window 08:18-08:30 UTC. They attached a CSV of raw latencies (lots of 1.2s spikes). They said our support dashboard p99 is flat.

Megan (eng-platform): Which metric name? Are they using the per-route rollup or the raw histogram? We have two panels for p99: route.p99.rollup and route.latency.histogram-derived.p99.

Sarah (support): They said "API > generation > p99" in the customer-facing dashboard (I think that maps to route.p99.rollup).

Jason (sre): OK. Quick hypothesis: if client is doing aggressive retries on auth failures, we can get retries counted as separate requests in the rollup but the histogram backend may drop 401s before bucketization. Need logs.

Alex (oncall): I pulled traces for that request_id — I see a lot of repeated auth failures (401) then a successful retry. Trace spans: auth proxy (150ms) -> retry -> model call (1.05s). The retries are inflating p99 on the aggregation that counts attempts.

Sarah (support): Here's the relevant lines from the app logs (redacted):
```
2024-04-22T08:19:03Z clip-req-9b7f3 auth: 401 token invalid client=clipper id=xx
2024-04-22T08:19:03Z clip-req-9b7f3 retry: attempt=2 backoff=120ms
2024-04-22T08:19:04Z clip-req-9b7f3 auth: 200 token accepted
2024-04-22T08:19:04Z clip-req-9b7f3 model.call latency_ms=1050 route=/v1/generate
```

Megan (eng-platform): That matches: customer sees slower p99 because each attempt counts toward rollup. Our histogram pipeline filters out auth failures (status!=200) before the latency bucket step — so histogram-derived p99 excludes retries. Different definitions.

Jason (sre): Also noticed our ingest sampler drops 75% of high-frequency short requests in the stats collector during spikes — that can hide tails in histogram panels. The rollup is counting attempts pre-sampling, histogram is post-sample.

Sarah (support): Customer is upset because SLA meter (they check p99) looked fine on our public dashboard. They want either correction or explanation + mitigation.

Alex (oncall): Short-term mitigation suggestions:
- Tell Clipper to turn off aggressive client retries (they use 2 retries with no jitter).
- Add a temporary rule to exclude auth-failure attempts from route.p99.rollup aggregation (need safe rollout).
- Add extra logging/tracing for a window to quantify retry amplification.

Megan (eng-platform): We can also add a panel showing "attempts vs successful requests" and a p99_successful metric to make this explicit. That's lower friction.

Jason (sre): Proposed action list:
1) Support: reply to customer explaining mismatch is due to retries being counted in rollup vs histogram filtering. Ask them to share client retry policy. (Sarah)
2) Eng-platform: add temporary p99_successful panel and a note in the dashboard doc clarifying definition. (Megan)
3) SRE: enable short-term increased sampling for histograms for that route between 08:00-09:00 UTC to capture tails for postmortem. (Jason)
4) Oncall: if amplification confirmed, throttle retries at API edge for that customer for next 30m. (Alex)

Sarah (support): I'll draft the customer message and ask for the retry config.

Megan (eng-platform): I'll add the panel and a tooltip explaining the difference by EOD. Quick snippet for the new metric mapping:
```yaml
metrics:
  - name: route.latency.p99_successful
    filter: status=200 and !retry_attempt
    source: histograms
```

Jason (sre): For sampling tweak — I'll flip the collector sampling flag for route=/v1/generate to 1.0 from 0.25 for 30 minutes. Doing now.

deploy-bot: deploy  - eng-platform/collector-sampling @ jason triggered (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:

Jason (sre): Sampling bump applied. Also added a temporary metric that increments only on retry events so we can quantify amplification.

Alex (oncall): If we need immediate protection, I can apply a per-customer retry-surface throttle at the edge: 3 attempts/min for Clipper. Prefer to coordinate with support first.

Sarah (support): Clipper replied: they run a third-party SDK that does 2 immediate retries on any 4xx/5xx, not aware. Asking if we can block retries server-side.

Megan (eng-platform): We should avoid breaking their SDK. Let's present options: 1) recommend SDK config change; 2) temporary server-side throttling for that customer; 3) long-term: make rollup metric exclude auth-failure attempts by default.

Jason (sre): Logged follow-up for postmortem: obs-definitions.md needs a section on "what counts for rollup vs histogram" and a checklist for customer-facing dashboards.

Alex (oncall): I'll hold off on throttling until support confirms. For now sampling bump + new panels should provide evidence.

Sarah (support): Customer acknowledged. They turned off SDK retries for a canary build — saw immediate drop in observed p99. They want the official explanation and dashboard update. I'll send formal RCA once we finish. :+1:

Megan (eng-platform): Great. I'll keep the new panel live and add the tooltip + doc link.

Jason (sre): Leaving the sampling bump for another 15m to gather data, then revert to baseline.

Sarah (support): Thanks all — will send the customer note now and close escalation once RCA is in their hands.

Alex (oncall): Nicely handled. Note for postmortem: add recommended dashboard naming conventions to avoid future confusion (e.g., p99_attempts vs p99_successful). :memo:
